hints: Focus on the reaction type here, a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol with concentrated sulfuric acid is the classic recipe for making an ester.
Remember how an ester is built, the acid part keeps its carbonyl carbon chain as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2$ from propanoic acid.
Now add the alcohol part, methanol contributes only a $\text{CH}_3$ group on the oxygen side, so join the two pieces together.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the reaction**

This is esterification. A carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol to form an ester plus water, with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ as catalyst.

$$\text{carboxylic acid + alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ester + water}$$

**Identify the two parts**

Propanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. Methanol is $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$. In the ester, the acid provides the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$ part and the alcohol provides the $\text{OCH}_3$ part.

**Join to make the ester**

Put them together and remove water to get methyl propanoate.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$, which is butan-2-one, a ketone. It has only one oxygen atom, but an ester must have the $\text{CO}_2$ group with two oxygens. It comes from forgetting the second oxygen in esterification.
options.B: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, methyl propanoate. The $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2$ part comes correctly from propanoic acid and the $\text{CH}_3$ part comes correctly from methanol. This is the expected esterification product.
options.C: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, ethyl ethanoate. It swaps the two reactants around, as if ethanoic acid reacted with ethanol. It is a trap for mixing up which part comes from the acid and which comes from the alcohol.
options.D: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, methyl butanoate. It has one extra $\text{CH}_2$ group, as if the acid was butanoic acid not propanoic acid. It is a trap for miscounting the three carbons in propanoic acid.
